newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle futures end lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle futures end lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed lower, pressured by a mix of fund and hedge selling in the June and August contracts, traders said.
Cash beef and cattle prices were under pressure late last week and early Tuesday packers bid steady to $1.00 lower.
"Cash is going to continue to erode because more numbers are coming," said Jim Clarkson, analyst with A and A Inc.

USDA Cattle on Feed Reports show that since March, nearly six percent more cattle were placed in feedlots than a year ago in the seven major cattle feeding states and many of these cattle will be sold this summer.
Clarkson said by July, cash cattle will likely be trading in the low $60 per cwt versus $66.00 sales on Friday.
